messages:
Maya: FYI we need to lock down the acceptance criteria for customer-managed firewall/NAT in private deploys. Customer asking for clear rollback steps and ownership — pinging eng + ops.

Liam: +1. Key question: do we require customer to provide static egress IPs, or do we support dynamic NAT with our egress pool?

Maya: Prefer to support both but acceptance must state which mode is used per customer. For v1 we should require one of: (a) customer static egress IPs, or (b) customer-managed NAT gateway with BGP advertised IPs.

Sanjay: Can we list explicit tests? e.g., inbound reachability to control-plane endpoints, egress port allowlist test, healthcheck path.

Maya: Yes. Draft acceptance checklist: 1) Control-plane handshake successful across VPN/VPC peering. 2) TLS mTLS cert exchange validated. 3) Egress IPs documented and routable (if static). 4) Our health ping (HEAD /health) returns 200 from customer subnet. 5) Inbound port rules enumerated and tested.

Emily: Also add a simulated failover test where customer withdraws routes and we automatically fall back to the hosted fallback model within 2m. Acceptance should include failover observability (traces + incident created).

Jeff: For rollback: if customer-side networking causes production errors, we need an immediate rollback path to Hosted fallback or Dedicated pool. Proposed steps: 1) Disable private route at our router (operator action). 2) Switch routing policy to hosted-fallback in Smart Routing UI. 3) Notify customer and run smoke tests.

Maya: Add exact commands and runbook lines. Minimal operator commands:```bash
# disable route to customer
redwoodctl networking disable-tenant-route --tenant-id=TENANT
# switch routing policy
redwoodctl routing set-policy --tenant TENANT --policy hosted-fallback
```

Sanjay: Can we also require that customer provides an out-of-band emergency contact and an API key to programmatically toggle on their side? If not, rollback will be slower.

Maya: Yes, put that as a nonfunctional requirement: emergency contact + out-of-band toggle OR documented scheduled maintenance window.

Liam: Edge case: customer behind symmetric NAT or carrier-grade NAT. That breaks BGP sessions and some control-plane callbacks. Acceptance should explicitly fail if symmetric NAT detected unless customer provides NAT hairpin solution.

Emily: Add test snippet to run from customer side to validate hairpin/NAT behavior:```bash
# from customer subnet
curl -ik https://cp.redwood.example.com/health -H 'Host: cp.redwood.example.com'
# should return 200 and a x-tenant header
```

Maya: Security note: require that any customer-managed firewall rule changes are logged and exported to our audit collector (or pushed to customer S3) for 90 days. Put this in compliance acceptance.

Jeff: Operational ownership: network onboarding is co-owned: Eng-Platform sets acceptance, Customer Success runs checklist with customer, Eng-Infra performs the operator actions for rollback. Document SLA for rollback time (TTR < 15m to route fallback after operator approval).

ops-bot: Deploy check: onboarding-runbook-v2 has been updated and published: https://internal.redwood/runbooks/onboarding-runbook-v2

Maya: Great. Next actions: Liam to write the PRD section for firewall/NAT expectations, Sanjay to expand test cases, Jeff to write rollback runbook steps verbatim. Aim for a PRD + RFC draft by EOD Friday. React with :thumbsup: when you picked it up.

Liam: I'll take PRD section. :thumbsup:

Sanjay: I'll do test cases. :thumbsup:

Jeff: I'll draft rollback steps and operator checklist. :thumbsup:

Emily: I'll add the failover observability requirements and a sample dashboard query.

Maya: Thanks all — leaving this thread as the single source for acceptance criteria. If you add major changes, please paste into the RFC doc.
